title: Ofgem publishes the energy price cap for 1 April to 30 June 2027 — the VAT snap-back is worth about GBP 45 (2.6% of the headline, not 5%), and the decision that sets it is the 2026-10-28 Budget, not this date
source: EST: THE PREFIX IS EXACT, NOT A TAXONOMY ARTIFACT — the primary states a CEILING, so the specific day is a reasoning estimate on top of a fetched primary. Ofgem's own October-cap release, ofgem.gov.uk/news/changes-energy-price-cap-between-1-october-and-31-december-2026 (published 26 August 2026, fetched direct 2026-09-09, HTTP 200), reads verbatim under 'Energy price cap level dates': '23 February 2027 - period 1 April 2027 to 30 June 2027'. The operative word in the list's stem is 'will be announced by', and Ofgem states the discretion on its sibling pages ('We may publish before this date if we need to because of external reasons'). THE FEBRUARY-SPECIFIC BASE RATE IS BETTER THAN THE POOLED ONE: the only early publication in the four cycles this lane and its sibling could source is a NOVEMBER cycle (by 25 Nov 2025, published 21 Nov 2025). Both sourceable FEBRUARY cycles landed ON the stated day — 25 February 2026 (Apr-Jun 2026, -7% to GBP 1,641) and 25 February 2025 (Apr-Jun 2025, +6.4% to GBP 1,849). February is 2 of 2 on the day; the pooled figure is 3 of 4. Honest caveat: the 25 February 2025 PUBLICATION date is sourced, but no prior release stating 'by 25 February 2025' as its ceiling was fetched, so that cycle is stronger evidence about the day than about the ceiling. Also filed estimate on this lane's no-self-confirm limit and because market-events-data.ts's confirmed-prefix taxonomy (IR:/CAL:/BLS:/FED:/PJM:/SEC:/TSY:/OCC:/BEA:/CENSUS:/ISM:/CB:/UMICH:/FHFA:) has no slot for a UK sector regulator. Proposed 2026-09-09 by the ofgem-price-cap-announcement-2026-11-25 lane; researched and made canonical by its own lane the same day
notes: CANONICAL FILE WRITTEN BY THE never-assessed INITIAL RESEARCH 2026-09-09, superseding proposals/ofgem-price-cap-announcement-2027-02-23.from-ofgem-price-cap-announcement-2026-11-25.json (read in full first, per docs/process/EVENT-RESEARCH.md). THE PROPOSER'S PLACEMENT AND ITS CENTRAL CLAIM BOTH SURVIVE — this is the first cap that must price domestic electricity back at 5% VAT, and that makes it the one cap announcement on this calendar carrying a mechanical tax component. THREE THINGS THE RESEARCH ADDED OR CORRECTED. (1) SIZED, FROM OFGEM'S OWN COUNTERFACTUAL. The proposal said 'a mechanical ~5% snap-back on the electricity leg'. That is right about the LEG and roughly double the effect on the HEADLINE, which is the number every reader will meet. Ofgem published the counterfactual itself in the 26 August 2026 press release (fetched direct 2026-09-09): 'Without the Government's intervention on VAT, this figure would have been around GBP 45 higher' — GBP 45 on the GBP 1,723 typical dual-fuel direct-debit cap is +2.61%. Cornwall Insight corroborates independently and from the other side (21 July 2026, fetched): 'Households are set to save around GBP 44 on a typical dual-fuel energy bill'. Two sources, GBP 44-45, implying a VAT-exclusive electricity leg near GBP 900, about 52% of the headline. THE SNAP-BACK IS ~GBP 45 / ~+2.6% OF HEADLINE, NOT ~5%. (2) THE DECOMPOSITION IS AVAILABLE ON THE DAY, WHICH REFUTES THE SIBLING'S STATED REASON FOR A CONTROL QUARTER. The 2026-11-25 ledger wrote that 'without the second one [the Jul-Sep 2027 cap] the April step cannot be decomposed into tax versus wholesale'. Ofgem quarterly releases routinely attribute the change to named components with pound figures — the Apr-Jun 2026 release (fetched) gives '-GBP 150' policy, '-GBP 38' wholesale, '+GBP 66' network — and the October release named the VAT effect in pounds unprompted. The Jul-Sep 2027 cap is still worth tracking as an out-of-sample check, but not because the April step is otherwise undecomposable. (3) THE DECISION IS NOT MADE ON THIS DATE, AND NOT BY OFGEM. Whether the snap-back happens at all turns on whether SI 2026/987 is extended, and the Government's own words scope that to the Budget: 'Any further action, including on funding for longer-term measures, will be taken at the Budget alongside an OBR forecast' (21 July 2026). The Budget is 2026-10-28 (tracked) — 118 days BEFORE this announcement. By 2027-02-23 the tax answer is roughly four months old and Ofgem is pricing a decision, not making one. THE RESIDUAL RISK WINDOW, STATED HONESTLY: an extension is a negative-procedure SI needing no vote and layable up to 2027-03-31 (established from primaries by the uk-electricity-vat-reversion-2027-04-01 lane), i.e. up to 36 DAYS AFTER Ofgem announces. If the Budget is silent, Ofgem announces a cap priced at 5% into a tax rate that could still change. No precedent for Ofgem revising an already-announced cap was located; that is an open limit, not a claim. TIMING: under Ofgem's 3-1.5-12[3] indexation the observation window closes 30 working days before the cap period, i.e. 2027-02-16 for a period starting 2027-04-01 (UK bank holidays Good Friday 2027-03-26 and Easter Monday 2027-03-29 are inside the count). The construction was VALIDATED rather than assumed: applied to the 1 January 2026 cap period it returns 2025-11-18, exactly the date Cornwall Insight published as that cycle's window close. So the number is arithmetic ~7 days before the announcement, and one day BEFORE the January 2027 UK CPI prints (2027-02-17, proposed). AN APRIL-SEASONALITY HYPOTHESIS TESTED AND KILLED: 'the April cap falls seasonally' does not hold — Apr-Jun 2025 rose 6.4% and Apr-Jun 2026 fell 7%, and the 2026 fall was driven by policy costs (-GBP 150), not season. A SECOND AGGREGATOR CLAIM REJECTED ON THE RECORD, after the sibling rejected one: a syndicated headline reports the October 2026 cap as 'GBP 1,935'. That is the OLD typical-consumption basis. Ofgem reduced TDCV in July 2026; reconstructing the published unit rates (electricity 26.32p/kWh + 54.83p/day standing, gas 7.97p/kWh + 29.68p/day) against the reduced consumption reproduces GBP 1,730, within GBP 7 of Ofgem's published GBP 1,723, while the old basis gives GBP 1,936. Any cross-cycle comparison in this file is on the post-July-2026 basis only. TIERED LOW on the same grounds as its sibling: symbols [], and this calendar's entire universe is eight US mega-caps (AAPL AMZN AVGO CRWV GOOG META MRVL MSFT) with no UK listing, utility, gilt or sterling instrument; no house playbook (S1/S2/E1/S3/S4/G1) is energy- or sterling-keyed. Estimate widens caution only; nothing date-keyed may act on this. Ledger: docs/research/events/ofgem-price-cap-announcement-2027-02-23.md
